hooks.prompt:
BEFORE exiting plan mode, you MUST complete a full plan review loop. This is automatic — do NOT skip it.

1. Spawn 2 review agents IN PARALLEL on the ENTIRE plan file (not just recent changes):
   - Agent A (Industry Design Checker): Read the full plan. Cross-check every design decision against CLAUDE.md conventions: zero-alloc hot path, Agrona collections (no java.util.*), fixed-point pricing (long x 10^-8), deterministic cluster (no wall-clock, no randomness), SBE/FIX field IDs, final var for reference types, explicit final for primitives, threading model on every class, Javadoc standards, clock discipline (injected EpochNanoClock/NanoClock), logging (GFLog hot-path, Log4j2 infra, no SLF4J). Flag anything that contradicts or omits these conventions.
   - Agent B (Completeness + Quality): Check for: missing edge cases, missing error handling, missing test plan, missing verification steps, vague language (should/might/consider), ambiguous instructions, incomplete module coverage, no TODO/TBD without Linear issue reference.

2. Fix ALL findings in the plan file. Nothing accepted, nothing out of scope (dev phase).

3. Re-run BOTH agents on the ENTIRE plan (not just changes). Loop until zero findings.

4. Print the plan compliance report (MEASURED, never guessed):
   Convention Alignment | Completeness | Testability | Error Handling | Threading Model | Allocation Model | Specificity
   Each scored PASS/SUBPAR/FAIL with actual finding counts.
   Accepted/Out-of-scope table (MUST be empty).

5. ONLY THEN proceed with ExitPlanMode.

Check if this Bash command is: (1) a git push to main — if it pushes directly to main (e.g. 'git push origin main', or 'git push' while on main branch), BLOCK it with 'No direct pushes to main — all changes must go via PRs'. (2) a git commit — verify the FULL command text contains 'APP-{N}: ' where N is a number (Linear issue reference) — note the commit message may span multiple lines in a heredoc. (3) creates a new branch (git checkout -b, git branch <name>, git switch -c) — verify the branch name matches 'feat/app-{N}-*' pattern. If the command is not related to git push/commit/branch creation, ALLOW it. If it violates a convention, BLOCK it with an explanation. Command: $ARGUMENTS

hooks.prompt:
A push just completed via make push. You MUST now poll for Gemini review and fix all findings:

1. Record PUSH_TIME=$(date -u -v-30S +%%Y-%%m-%%dT%%H:%%M:%%SZ) (30s clock-skew buffer)
2. Wait for Gemini review: poll every 30s until gemini-code-assist[bot] review appears
3. Fetch ALL Gemini line-level comments created after PUSH_TIME
4. Fix ALL high, medium, and low severity findings
5. If fixes made: run spotlessApply, commit, run all 3 test suites, push again (which triggers another Gemini round)
6. Loop until Gemini has zero actionable comments

Do NOT skip this. Do NOT say 'I already pushed'. Do NOT move on without polling Gemini. This is MANDATORY after every push.
hooks.statusMessage: Enforcing Gemini review poll after push...

[ "$EXIT_CODE" -eq 0 ] && jq -nc '{decision:"block", reason:"A git commit just completed. You MUST now run ALL three test suites before pushing or doing anything else:

  1. ./gradlew test
  2. ./gradlew :integration-tests:test
  3. ./gradlew e2e

Do NOT skip any suite. Do NOT claim they were already run. Execute each command and report results."}' || exit 0
